attempted_claim: Let (T_N,e_N) be a free Boltzmann type-I triangulation with simple boundary of perimeter ℓ_N, where ℓ_N/√N→1. Split the boundary at a root edge and a target edge into left and right arcs with ℓ_N^L/√N→ℓ_L∈(0,1) and ℓ_N^R/√N→1−ℓ_L. Put Bernoulli bond percolation with p_c=(2√3−1)/11 on the interior edges, make the left boundary arc open and the right boundary arc closed (Dobrushin boundary data), and let λ_N be the canonical medial exploration path separating the two boundary states, linearly interpolated in the metric realization of the map. Is there a deterministic a_b>0 such that (T_N,(3/2)N^(−1/4)d_gr,(3/4)N^(−1)∑_{v∈V(T_N)}deg(v)δ_v,λ_N(a_bN^(3/4)·)) converges in law in the Gromov–Hausdorff–Prokhorov–uniform topology to (𝓑,d_𝓑,μ_𝓑,η), where 𝓑 is the unit-perimeter free Brownian disk with the two marked boundary points and, conditionally on 𝓑, η is chordal SLE_6 from the first mark to the second, parametrized by quantum natural time?
decisive_failure: Lane-scale derivation cannot supply the missing uniform percolation-on-random-map inputs (RSW, Cardy observable, exact Dobrushin bond-peeling kernels, joint quantum-clock convergence); result is obstacle localization only, not a partial convergence theorem.
